mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes E Class 250 petrol turbo engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only rebuilt M274 engines range from £2,800 to £5,500 depending on engine code and condition. With specialist fitting, budget £3,200-£6,300 total. M274.920 (E 200, 184 hp / E 250, 211 hp, 2013-2017): rebuilt £2,800-£4,500. M274.930/940 (E 200 / E 250, 2016-2023): rebuilt £3,200-£5,500. Labour adds £400-£800 depending on specialist location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in an E Class 200 petrol turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cold-start rattling that disappears after a few seconds is the classic early warning sign. On the M274, timing chain wear typically occurs around 80,000 miles. Rattling noise on cold start, particularly from the front of the engine. Metallic clanging sounds from the timing chain area. Loss of power or engine misfires. Timing chain replacement at a specialist costs £1,000-£1,800.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on an E Class 250 petrol turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the car is otherwise sound. W213 E 250 petrol turbo examples with good service history command £10,000-£25,000 used, making replacement viable. A quality rebuilt M274 costs £2,800-£5,500 supply only. The M274 is a desirable engine with strong performance and refinement. A replacement engine with warranty costs less than the depreciation on a newer car. Specialist fitting adds £400-£800, not dealer rates of £1,500+.

mainEntity.name: What causes piston cracking in the M274 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low-speed pre-ignition (LSPI) combined with oil dilution causes detonation events that crack pistons between ring lands. There is no preventative fix - once a piston cracks, the engine must be rebuilt or replaced. Piston failure typically occurs between 50,000-90,000 miles. No warning signs - failure is sudden and catastrophic. Rebuilt engines with forged pistons eliminate the repeat failure risk. Using high-quality fuel and regular oil changes may reduce LSPI risk.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the E 200 and E 250 petrol turbo engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both use the same M274 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder engine - the E 250 is a higher-output tune producing 211 hp (vs 184 hp) and 350 Nm (vs 300 Nm). E 200: 135 kW (184 hp), 300 Nm - 0-62 mph in 7.5 seconds. E 250: 155 kW (211 hp), 350 Nm - 0-62 mph in 6.9 seconds. Both share the same 1,991 cc displacement and M274 architecture. Both suffer from the same timing chain, piston, and thermostat issues.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes E Class 250 petrol turbo engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance and 8,000-10,000 mile oil changes, M274 engines regularly reach 150,000-200,000 miles. Timing chain replacement at 80k-100k miles is recommended. M274 is a modern, efficient engine with a robust bottom end. Timing chain inspection/replacement at 80k-100k miles is recommended. Thermostat replacement at 40k-80k miles prevents cooling issues. Short oil change intervals (8k miles) are critical for timing chain and piston life.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz E Class 200 / 250 Petrol Turbo - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The E 200 and E 250 petrol turbo badges represented Mercedes-Benz's entry-level and mid-range petrol offerings across the W212 and W213 E-Class generations. Both used the M274 2.0-litre turbocharged inline-four engine - a modern, direct-injection unit that replaced the supercharged M271. The M274 delivered strong performance and efficiency, but carried a reputation for timing chain wear, piston cracking, and thermostat failures that has made it a significant replacement candidate in the UK used market.

milestones.description: **2013** - W212 facelift E 200 launched with M274.920 2.0-litre turbo, 135 kW (184 hp), 300 Nm
**2013** - W212 facelift E 250 launched with M274.920 2.0-litre turbo, 155 kW (211 hp), 350 Nm
**2016** - W213 E 200 and E 250 launched with updated M274.920 / M274.930 engines
**2017** - M274 replaced by M264 engine family in newer E-Class models
**2016-2023** - W213 E 200 (184 hp) and E 250 (211 hp) petrol turbo models produced

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes E Class 200 / 250 Petrol Turbo Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The M274 engine that powers the E Class 200 and 250 petrol turbo is a modern, efficient unit that delivers strong performance - but its reputation for timing chain wear, piston cracking, and thermostat failure has made it a significant replacement candidate in the UK used market. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down what these failures cost to fix and when replacement is the smarter option.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - Why the M274 in the E Class 200 / 250 Petrol Turbo Fails Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes E Class 200 / 250 Petrol Turbo (M274.920 / M274.930 / M274.940, 2013-2023)
problems.rootCause: The M274's timing chain and tensioner wear over time, particularly when oil change intervals are extended beyond 10,000 miles. Cold-start rattling is the classic early warning sign. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, bending valves and destroying the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain tensioner only
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-80,000 miles; effective if rattle is minimal

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has stretched or rattle persists

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt M274 with new timing components and upgraded parts
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has jumped causing valvetrain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W212 E 200 or E 250 petrol turbo is worth £4,000-£10,000 depending on condition and mileage; a W213 example commands £10,000-£25,000【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. Given the strong residual value of these models - particularly W213 examples - a rebuilt engine with warranty is almost always justifiable if the rest of the car is sound.
problems.recommendation: The cold-start rattle is your early warning - don't ignore it. A specialist timing chain replacement at £1,000-£1,800 is significantly cheaper than the £3,000+ valvetrain rebuild if the chain jumps. Given the £10,000+ value of most W213 E 250 examples, preventative chain work is a wise investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M274 Mercedes E Class 200 / 250 petrol turbo engine prices

problems.h4: Piston Cracking - The M274 Catastrophic Failure
problems.rootCause: Low-speed pre-ignition (LSPI) combined with oil dilution causes detonation events that crack pistons between ring lands. This is a well-documented issue on the M274 engine. There is no preventative fix - once a piston cracks, the engine must be rebuilt or replaced.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or reconditioned short block fitted with existing ancillaries
repairOptions.longevity: 50,000-90,000 miles; cranks and pistons new, head reused

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of fully rebuilt M274 with forged pistons and upgraded rings
repairOptions.longevity: 100,000+ miles; stronger pistons prevent repeat failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of low-mileage used M274 from salvage
repairOptions.longevity: 50,000-80,000 miles; no upgrade - same design flaw remains

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W212 £4,000-£10,000; W213 £10,000-£25,000). On a W213 worth £15,000+, a specialist-supplied rebuilt engine with forged pistons costs marginally more than a used replacement but eliminates the repeat failure risk. Avoid dealer pricing here - the premium buys no design improvement.
problems.recommendation: There is no minor repair for a cracked piston - the engine must come apart. On a W213 E 250 petrol turbo worth £15,000+, a specialist-supplied rebuilt engine with forged pistons is the only sensible choice. The M274's piston cracking is a design weakness that used engines do not address - only a rebuilt unit with upgraded pistons eliminates the repeat failure risk.
problems.cta: -> Compare M274 Mercedes E Class 200 / 250 petrol turbo rebuilt engine prices

problems.h4: Thermostat Failure & Cooling System Issues - The M274 Common Weakness
problems.rootCause: The thermostat is a common failure point on the M274. Its location under the engine makes replacement labour-intensive (approximately 3 hours). A failed thermostat prevents the engine from reaching operating temperature, increasing fuel consumption and emissions. Extended exposure to incorrect temperatures can contribute to LSPI and piston damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of thermostat and coolant refill
Replacement of thermostat, water pump and coolant
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000+ miles; addresses related cooling system components

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt M274 with new cooling components
repairOptions.longevity: When overheating has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W212 £4,000-£10,000; W213 £10,000-£25,000). At £250-£450, thermostat replacement is a relatively minor expense to protect a high-value asset.
problems.recommendation: The thermostat is a known weak point - if you notice the temperature gauge taking longer than usual to reach normal operating temperature, or if fuel consumption has increased, have it inspected. The £250-£450 specialist replacement is far cheaper than the engine damage that prolonged incorrect operating temperatures can cause. Combine with a water pump replacement at higher mileages to avoid repeat labour.
problems.cta: -> Get M274 Mercedes E Class 200 / 250 petrol turbo thermostat and cooling quotes

problems.h4: Camshaft Adjuster & PCV System Failure - The M274 Top-End Issues
problems.rootCause: Camshaft adjusters (solenoids) wear, typically after 60-70k miles, causing noise on cold start. The PCV system can fail, causing increased crankcase pressure, check engine lights, fuel vapour smell, and potential long-term turbo issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: PCV valve and breather system replacement
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000+ miles; addresses oil leaks and pressure issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt M274 with new adjusters and PCV components
repairOptions.longevity: When adjuster failure has caused valvetrain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W212 £4,000-£10,000; W213 £10,000-£25,000). At £300-£550, camshaft adjuster replacement is a manageable expense to protect a high-value asset.
problems.recommendation: Camshaft adjuster noise on cold start is a common M274 issue - 2014-onwards engines received modified actuators that hold longer. If you hear unusual top-end noise, have it inspected promptly. The PCV system is a known design defect acknowledged by Mercedes - early replacement prevents costly turbo and engine damage.
